title: Private LLM Hosting on Kubernetes with LiteLLM, Langfuse & Netdata
subtitle: Self-hosted Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct inference cluster orchestrated via LiteLLM Gateway, NextChat UI, Langfuse LLM observability, and Netdata real-time hardware telemetry.

overview.summary: An enterprise-grade, privacy-first LLM hosting platform running on Kubernetes. Serves the high-performance Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct model behind an intelligent LiteLLM proxy, fronted by NextChat UI, tracked comprehensively by Langfuse for prompt/token telemetry, and monitored in real time via Netdata.
overview.problemStatement: Commercial LLM APIs introduce recurring per-token expenses, vendor lock-in, data privacy hazards, and opaque latency spikes. Deploying raw self-hosted models without a unified gateway, session tracking, and hardware telemetry leads to unmanaged token exhaustion and operational blind spots.
corePrinciples: Zero Data Leakage: Complete control over inference workloads with in-cluster model execution.
Unified LiteLLM Proxying: Standardized OpenAI-compatible API interface with key budgeting, rate limiting, and automated Langfuse callbacks.
Dual-Plane Observability: Langfuse for LLM traces/token analytics and Netdata for per-second CPU/GPU/memory hardware diagnostics.
Frictionless User Experience: NextChat web and mobile UI delivering sub-50ms streaming token generation.

data.label: NextChat UI
data.subtitle: chat.devutkarsh.com
data.description: Modern, lightweight chat client delivering real-time streaming conversations, system prompt customization, and multi-session management. Accessible live at chat.devutkarsh.com/#/.
responsibilities: Renders real-time markdown, code highlighting, and streaming responses
Maintains client-side chat histories and custom system prompts
Sends authenticated completions to the LiteLLM gateway
Supports dark mode, responsive layout, and one-click session export
failureModes: SSE stream disconnection on network disruption
Local storage quota exhaustion for conversation history

configSnippet.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nextchat-ui
  namespace: llm-platform
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nextchat-ui
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nextchat-ui
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nextchat
        image: yidadaa/chatgpt-next-web:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: BASE_URL
          value: "https://gateway.devutkarsh.com/v1"
        - name: OPENAI_API_KEY
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: litellm-keys
              key: master-key

data.label: LiteLLM AI Gateway
data.subtitle: gateway.devutkarsh.com
data.description: High-throughput OpenAI-compatible proxy routing requests to in-cluster Qwen 2.5 3B engines, enforcing rate limits, virtual keys, and automatic Langfuse telemetry hooks. Demo access: tester@devutkarsh.com / Tester@123456.
responsibilities: Translates standard OpenAI API requests to local model endpoints
Enforces team API keys, spend budgets, and rate limiting
Asynchronously forwards generation metrics to Langfuse
Provides management UI and virtual key generation at gateway.devutkarsh.com
failureModes: Upstream model pod saturation causing timeout errors
PostgreSQL connection exhaustion during sudden traffic spikes

configSnippet.code:
model_list:
  - model_name: qwen-2.5-3b-instruct
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/qwen2.5-3b
      api_base: http://qwen-inference-service.llm-platform.svc:8000/v1
      api_key: "EMPTY"
litellm_settings:
  callbacks:
    - langfuse
  success_callback:
    - langfuse
  failure_callback:
    - langfuse

data.label: Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct Engine
data.subtitle: Kubernetes Inference Pod
data.description: High-performance inference engine running Alibaba's Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct model. Provides blazingly fast reasoning, code generation, and low-latency token streaming.
responsibilities: Executes parallelized tensor operations with KV cache reuse
Generates streaming token responses with low time-to-first-token
Serves OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint internally
Manages dynamic batching for concurrent prompt evaluations
failureModes: GPU Out-Of-Memory (OOM) during extreme context window usage
Context length truncation for prompts exceeding maximum sequence limit

configSnippet.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: qwen-inference
  namespace: llm-platform
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: model-server
        image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
        args:
        - "--model"
        - "Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct"
        - "--port"
        - "8000"
        - "--max-model-len"
        - "8192"
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: 16Gi

data.label: Langfuse LLM Tracing
data.subtitle: langfuse.devutkarsh.com
data.description: Comprehensive LLM observability and evaluation platform tracking traces, token consumption, latency breakdowns, and prompt revisions. Demo login: tester@devutkarsh.com / Tester@123456.
responsibilities: Visualizes end-to-end user request traces and execution graphs
Calculates token counts, generation latencies, and estimated cost savings
Monitors model quality, output evaluations, and user feedback
Provides analytics dashboard and query console at langfuse.devutkarsh.com
failureModes: Trace ingestion queue lag during burst workloads
Database storage growth requiring log retention pruning

configSnippet.code:
env:
  - name: LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY
    value: "pk-lf-prod-k8s-mesh"
  - name: LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: langfuse-secrets
        key: secret-key
  - name: LANGFUSE_HOST
    value: "https://langfuse.devutkarsh.com"

data.label: Netdata Telemetry
data.subtitle: netdata.devutkarsh.com
data.description: Real-time, per-second node and container infrastructure metrics dashboard. Monitor GPU VRAM, CPU load, and network I/O. (Note: Click 'Skip' / 'Explore without sign in' to view dashboard directly).
responsibilities: Collects high-frequency 1-second interval hardware telemetry
Monitors GPU temperature, VRAM allocation, and CUDA compute saturation
Tracks Kubernetes pod memory limits and CPU throttling
Provides interactive real-time charts at netdata.devutkarsh.com (no sign-in required)
failureModes: eBPF sensor permission constraints on restricted kernel nodes
Browser rendering lag when streaming 1,000+ real-time metric charts simultaneously

configSnippet.code:
apiVersion: helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2beta1
kind: HelmRelease
metadata:
  name: netdata
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  chart:
    spec:
      chart: netdata
      version: 3.7.x
  values:
    k8sState:
      enabled: true
    parent:
      database:
        persistence: true

data.label: PostgreSQL & Redis DB
data.subtitle: State & Virtual Key Store
data.description: In-cluster relational database powering LiteLLM virtual key management, user quotas, spend tracking, and Langfuse state storage.
responsibilities: Persists LiteLLM virtual keys, rate limits, and team token usage
Stores Langfuse trace metadata, user tags, and scores
Provides low-latency session caching via Redis
failureModes: Disk IOPS saturation during high trace volume writes
Storage volume capacity alerts requiring PVC expansion

data.description: NextChat streams prompt payloads to LiteLLM Gateway and receives Server-Sent Events (SSE) token chunks in real time.
LiteLLM resolves the model alias and proxies the token generation request directly to the Qwen 2.5 3B inference engine pod.
LiteLLM automatically triggers callback hooks to send trace data, token counts, and generation timestamps to Langfuse asynchronously.

tradeoffs.chosenApproach: LiteLLM Proxy deployed as a centralized K8s service
pros: Provides OpenAI-compatible API interface for seamless client compatibility
Native plug-and-play callbacks for Langfuse without altering client apps
Centralized virtual key generation, rate limiting, and team budgeting
cons: Adds an additional hop (approx. 4-5ms) in the network path
Requires maintaining a PostgreSQL database for stateful key storage
rejectedAlternatives: Connecting NextChat directly to the raw vLLM pod (lacks rate limits and observability hooks)
Custom reverse proxy written from scratch (high maintenance overhead)

pros: Exceptional reasoning and instruction-following quality relative to its compact 3B footprint
Runs comfortably on modest GPU (4-8GB VRAM) or multi-core CPU instances
Zero per-token API charges and 100% data privacy compliance
cons: Requires managing GPU node pools and cluster auto-scaling
Smaller context window retention compared to 70B+ parameter models
rejectedAlternatives: Proprietary cloud APIs like GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 (high ongoing token costs and data residency concerns)
Running unquantized 70B parameter models (requires expensive multi-GPU clusters)

tradeoffs.chosenApproach: Dual-plane architecture: Langfuse for LLM traces + Netdata for real-time infrastructure
pros: Langfuse captures prompt semantics, token usage, latency percentiles, and evaluations
Netdata provides sub-second live hardware telemetry (VRAM, CPU, I/O) without sign-in friction
Decoupled operational layers allow debugging application vs infrastructure issues independently
cons: Two separate web dashboards to consult during deep incident investigations
rejectedAlternatives: Prometheus/Grafana only (misses prompt-level LLM execution traces and token semantics)
Langfuse only (lacks per-second hardware/GPU thermal and memory bandwidth metrics)

securityAndCompliance.implementation: All user prompts and generated model tokens remain strictly confined within the Kubernetes cluster private network. No external API calls are made.
LiteLLM enforces hashed virtual API keys with granular token budgets, expiration timestamps, and per-user rate limits.
All public ingress endpoints (chat.devutkarsh.com, gateway.devutkarsh.com, langfuse.devutkarsh.com, netdata.devutkarsh.com) are secured via cert-manager Let's Encrypt TLS certificates.
LiteLLM and Langfuse dashboards enforce authenticated credentials (tester@devutkarsh.com / Tester@123456), while Netdata provides read-only telemetry exploration.
